accused.ex: She accused her brother of taking her phone.

achieved.ex: She achieved her goal of running a marathon.

acknowledge.ex: She acknowledged that the plan had problems.

action.ex: The nurses voted for strike action.

addition.en: in addition to: as well as
addition.ex: In addition to French, she speaks Italian.

addressed.ex: The parcel was addressed to my neighbour.

admit.en: agree that something bad is true
admit.ex: He admits that he made a mistake.

agreement.ex: The two countries signed a trade agreement.

alleged.en: said someone did wrong, without proof
alleged.ex: The report alleged that the money was misused.

allocated.ex: Each team was allocated a room.

example.en: More money was allocated to the library this year.
example.zh: 今年撥給圖書館更多經費。

note.meaning: 「撥給、分配」，把資金或資源指定用於某用途。
note.usage: 常用 allocate A to B / for B；被動 be allocated 很常見。

noteEn.usage: Used as 'allocate something to/for something'; often passive.

noteEs.exampleTr: Este año se asignó más dinero a la biblioteca.
noteEs.meaning: Asignar dinero o recursos a un fin.
noteEs.usage: Se usa «allocate A to B»; la pasiva es frecuente.

noteHi.exampleTr: इस साल पुस्तकालय को अधिक धन आवंटित किया गया।
noteHi.meaning: किसी उद्देश्य के लिए धन या संसाधन देना।
noteHi.usage: allocate A to B; कर्मवाच्य be allocated आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 今年は図書館により多くの資金が割り当てられた。
noteJa.meaning: 資金などを特定の目的に「割り当てる、配分する」。
noteJa.usage: allocate A to B の形。受け身 be allocated も多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 올해 도서관에 더 많은 예산이 배정되었다.
noteKo.usage: allocate A to B 형태이며 수동태 be allocated도 흔하다.

allocation.en: an amount given for a purpose
allocation.ex: The school's budget allocation was cut.

example.en: Each class receives a small allocation for books.
example.zh: 每個班級都有一小筆買書的撥款。

note.meaning: 「撥款、分配額」，指被分配的一筆資金或資源。
note.usage: 可數名詞；常與 budget、funding 連用，如 budget allocation。

noteEn.meaning: An amount of money given for a purpose.

noteEs.exampleTr: Cada clase recibe una pequeña asignación para libros.
noteEs.meaning: Cantidad de dinero o recursos asignada a algo.

noteHi.exampleTr: हर कक्षा को किताबों के लिए थोड़ी राशि मिलती है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी उद्देश्य के लिए दी गई राशि; आवंटन।
noteHi.usage: गणनीय संज्ञा; budget allocation जैसे रूपों में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 各クラスには本のための少額の予算が配分される。
noteJa.meaning: 割り当てられた資金や資源、「配分（額）」。
noteJa.usage: 可算名詞。budget allocation の形でよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 각 반은 도서 구입을 위한 소액 예산을 받는다.
noteKo.usage: 셀 수 있는 명사로 budget allocation처럼 자주 쓴다.

answered.ex: She answered my email the same day.

appointment.en: choosing someone for a job or role
appointment.ex: The appointment of a new coach surprised fans.

are.en: exist or have a quality; also helps form verbs
are.ex: They are teachers at a local school.

argued.en: gave reasons to show something is true
argued.ex: He argued that the plan was too expensive.

arrived.ex: The reply arrived late in the evening.

as.en: in the role or way of

aside.en: to one side (set aside: keep for a purpose)
aside.ex: She set aside some money every month.

asked.ex: My boss asked me to stay late.

asserts.en: says firmly that something is true
asserts.ex: He asserts that the rules are unfair.

assurances.ex: They gave us assurances about job security.

at.en: in or near a place or time

attempt.ex: His first attempt at baking was a disaster.

attend.en: go to an event or meeting
attend.ex: Please attend the meeting on Friday.

auspices.en: support and control of an organisation
auspices.ex: The event was held under the auspices of the UN.
auspices.zh: 主持（under the auspices of：在…主持下）

avoidable.en: could have been stopped from happening

awards.en: pay increases that are officially agreed
awards.ex: The nurses received two pay awards last year.

basis.en: on a … basis: in a … way
basis.ex: We meet on a weekly basis.
basis.zh: on an annual basis：每年一次

be.en: exist or have a quality; also helps form verbs
be.ex: I want to be a doctor.

being.zh: 正在被（被動進行助動詞）

between.en: in the space or time separating two things

bid.ex: The team made a late bid to win the game.

bridge.en: reduce a difference between two things
bridge.ex: Extra classes can help bridge the learning gap.

bringing.en: bring in: ask someone to come and help
bringing.ex: Bringing in an expert saved us time.

broken.en: failed to keep (a promise); stopped working
broken.ex: He has broken his promise again.
broken.zh: 違背；破裂（break promises：違背承諾；break down：破裂）

brought.en: bring in: ask to come and help
brought.ex: A new manager was brought in last year.

budget.ex: The government announced its budget on Tuesday.

budgetary.ex: The school faces budgetary problems this year.

calling.ex: They are calling off the match because of rain.

came.ex: All our plans came to nothing.

cause.ex: Ice on the road can cause accidents.

cautioned.ex: The doctor cautioned him against eating too much salt.

cent.ex: Prices rose by five per cent.

chaired.en: led a meeting or group as chair
chaired.ex: The meeting was chaired by the head teacher.

change.ex: There has been no change in the price.

changed.ex: My city has changed a lot.

characterised.en: described as having a certain quality
characterised.ex: Critics characterised the film as boring.

close.en: make a gap smaller or end it
close.ex: The new rules aim to close the pay gap.

collapse.ex: The collapse of the deal shocked investors.

commission.en: an official group with a task; the EU executive
commission.ex: The European Commission proposed new rules.

commitment.en: a promise to give money or effort
commitment.ex: The city made a big commitment to new parks.

commitments.ex: The company met all its commitments to staff.

committed.en: promised to give effort to something
committed.ex: Both teams committed to playing fair.

committee.en: a group chosen to do a task
committee.ex: The committee will decide next week.

concede.en: admit something is true, often unwillingly
concede.ex: He had to concede that she was right.

concerned.ex: The book is concerned with family life.

congress.en: Congress (part of a union body's name)

consequently.ex: He missed the bus and consequently was late.

example.en: It snowed heavily; consequently, the school closed.
example.zh: 雪下得很大，因此學校停課了。

note.meaning: 「因此、所以」，引出前述情況的結果。
note.usage: 正式連接副詞，常置句首或動詞前，句首時後加逗號。

noteEn.usage: A formal linking word, often at the start of a sentence.

noteEs.exampleTr: Nevó mucho; por consiguiente, la escuela cerró.
noteEs.usage: Adverbio formal; suele ir al inicio de la oración seguido de coma.

noteHi.exampleTr: भारी बर्फ़ गिरी; परिणामस्वरूप स्कूल बंद हो गया।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक; वाक्य की शुरुआत में या क्रिया से पहले आता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 大雪が降った。その結果、学校は休校になった。
noteJa.usage: 改まった接続副詞で、文頭（後にコンマ）や動詞の前に置く。

noteKo.exampleTr: 눈이 많이 와서 그 결과 학교가 문을 닫았다.
noteKo.usage: 격식 있는 접속부사로 문장 앞이나 동사 앞에 둔다.

considerable.ex: The project cost a considerable amount of money.

considered.ex: The road is considered safe now.

contended.ex: She contended that the test was unfair.

contingent.ex: The trip is contingent on good weather.

example.en: Your place on the team is contingent on passing the exam.
example.zh: 你能否留在隊上取決於能否通過考試。

note.meaning: 「取決於、視…而定」，表示某事要以另一件事為前提。
note.usage: 常用 be contingent on/upon + 名詞，屬正式用語。

noteEn.usage: Formal; used in the pattern 'contingent on/upon something'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Tu lugar en el equipo depende de aprobar el examen.
noteEs.meaning: Que depende de otra cosa; supeditado a algo.
noteEs.usage: Se usa en registro formal con «contingent on/upon».

noteHi.exampleTr: टीम में तुम्हारी जगह परीक्षा पास करने पर निर्भर है।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर be contingent on/upon के साथ औपचारिक भाषा में।

noteJa.exampleTr: チームに残れるかは試験に合格するかどうか次第だ。
noteJa.meaning: 他の事柄「次第の、～を条件とする」。
noteJa.usage: be contingent on/upon の形で、改まった場面で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 네가 팀에 남는 것은 시험 통과 여부에 달려 있다.
noteKo.usage: 격식체에서 be contingent on/upon 형태로 쓴다.

continue.ex: The rain will continue all day.

convening.en: bringing people together for a meeting
convening.ex: The mayor is convening a meeting on traffic.

correspondence.ex: Keep all correspondence with the bank.

cost.en: cost of living: money needed for basic things
cost.ex: The cost of food keeps rising.

course.en: run its course: continue until it ends
course.ex: Let the illness run its course.
course.zh: 進程（run its course：自然結束）

court.en: a place where legal cases are decided
court.ex: She works as a clerk at the local court.

courts.en: places where legal cases are decided
courts.ex: The courts are very busy this month.

crux.ex: Money is the crux of the problem.

days.ex: We stayed there for three days.

deal.ex: The two sides finally made a deal.

department.en: a part of a government or organisation
department.ex: He works in the health department.

described.ex: She described the hotel as dirty.

deteriorate.ex: Old photos deteriorate in strong sunlight.

example.en: The weather deteriorated quickly in the afternoon.

note.meaning: 「惡化、變差」，指情況、品質或價值逐漸下降。
note.usage: 不及物動詞，不接受詞；in real terms 時指實質價值縮水。

noteEn.usage: It has no object: things deteriorate, you don't deteriorate them.

noteEs.exampleTr: El tiempo empeoró rápidamente por la tarde.
noteEs.usage: Verbo intransitivo; no lleva objeto directo.

noteHi.exampleTr: दोपहर में मौसम जल्दी बिगड़ गया।
noteHi.usage: अकर्मक क्रिया है; इसके बाद कर्म नहीं आता।

noteJa.exampleTr: 午後になって天気が急に悪化した。
noteJa.usage: 自動詞で目的語をとらない。

deteriorated.ex: Her health deteriorated during the winter.

example.en: The weather deteriorated quickly in the afternoon.

note.meaning: 「惡化、變差」，指情況、品質或價值逐漸下降。
note.usage: 不及物動詞，不接受詞；in real terms 時指實質價值縮水。

noteEn.usage: It has no object: things deteriorate, you don't deteriorate them.

noteEs.exampleTr: El tiempo empeoró rápidamente por la tarde.
noteEs.usage: Verbo intransitivo; no lleva objeto directo.

noteHi.exampleTr: दोपहर में मौसम जल्दी बिगड़ गया।
noteHi.usage: अकर्मक क्रिया है; इसके बाद कर्म नहीं आता।

noteJa.exampleTr: 午後になって天気が急に悪化した。
noteJa.usage: 自動詞で目的語をとらない。

discrepancy.en: a difference between things that should match
discrepancy.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.

example.en: There was a discrepancy between the bill and the receipt.
example.zh: 帳單和收據之間有出入。

note.meaning: 「差距、不一致」，指本應相符的兩者之間有差異。
note.usage: 常用 a discrepancy between A and B；可數名詞。

noteEn.meaning: A difference between things that should be the same.
noteEn.usage: Often used as 'a discrepancy between A and B'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Había una discrepancia entre la factura y el recibo.
noteEs.meaning: Diferencia entre dos cosas que deberían coincidir.
noteEs.usage: Se usa a menudo como «a discrepancy between A and B».

noteHi.exampleTr: बिल और रसीद के बीच अंतर था।
noteHi.meaning: दो चीज़ों के बीच अंतर जिन्हें मेल खाना चाहिए।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर a discrepancy between A and B के रूप में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 請求書と領収書の間に食い違いがあった。
noteJa.meaning: 一致すべきもの同士の「食い違い、差」。
noteJa.usage: a discrepancy between A and B の形でよく使う。可算名詞。

noteKo.usage: 주로 a discrepancy between A and B 형태로 쓴다.

discussions.ex: Discussions about the new park continue.

dispute.ex: The pay dispute lasted three months.

disruption.en: a break that stops normal activity
disruption.ex: The storm caused disruption to train services.

down.en: part of phrases: break down, turn down
down.ex: Their friendship broke down after the fight.

earmarked.ex: The money is earmarked for new schools.

earnings.ex: His earnings rose after the promotion.

education.ex: Higher education is free for some students.

effectively.ex: The shop is effectively closed now.

efforts.ex: Thanks for your efforts on the project.

eleventh-hour.en: happening at the last possible moment
eleventh-hour.ex: An eleventh-hour goal saved the team.

emphasised.en: said strongly that something is important
emphasised.ex: The coach emphasised the need for teamwork.

engage.ex: We want both sides to engage in dialogue.

engagement.ex: Close engagement with parents helps schools.

enshrined.ex: Free speech is enshrined in the constitution.

enter.ex: The two firms will enter talks next month.

eroded.ex: Rising prices have eroded our savings.

excess.ex: The bill was in excess of £500.

expected.ex: We expect the results on Monday.

failed.en: did not do what was expected
failed.ex: He failed to call his mother.

failing.ex: He was blamed for failing to call.

falls.en: falls short of: is less than
falls.ex: His score falls short of the top mark.

far.ex: This bag is far too heavy.

faster.ex: Prices are rising faster than wages.

follow.ex: More rain will follow this week.

fulfil.en: do what was promised or required
fulfil.ex: He fulfilled his promise to visit.

fundamental.ex: There is a fundamental problem with the plan.

further.ex: She further said that costs would rise.

furthermore.ex: The hotel is cheap. Furthermore, it is near the beach.

fórsa.ja: Fórsa（アイルランドの公務員労組）

gap.ex: The gap between rich and poor is growing.

general.ex: She became general manager last year.

get.en: cause something to start or happen

go.en: go on strike: stop working as protest
go.ex: The drivers may go on strike next week.

gone.en: go to great lengths: try very hard
gone.ex: She has gone to great lengths to help.

good.ex: There's a good reason for the delay.

government.en: the group of people who rule a country

grounds.ex: There are no grounds for complaint.

guarantee.en: a promise that something will happen
guarantee.ex: There is no guarantee of success.

hard.ex: She studied hard for the test.

health.ex: The health service is under pressure.

healthcare.ex: She wants a career in healthcare.

heart.en: centre (at the heart of: most involved in)
heart.ex: The hotel is at the heart of the city.
heart.ja: 中心（at the heart of：〜の中心に）
heart.zh: 核心（at the heart of：處於核心）

help.ex: The family needed help with rent.

honour.ex: The firm promised to honour all orders.

hospitals.en: places where sick people are treated
hospitals.ex: Hospitals are very busy in winter.

hour.ex: The train leaves in an hour.

however.ex: It was cold. However, we went out.

impasse.en: a situation where no progress is possible
impasse.ex: The talks have reached an impasse.

example.en: The two friends reached an impasse over holiday plans.
example.zh: 兩個朋友在假期計畫上陷入僵局。

note.meaning: 「僵局」，指雙方無法取得進展的狀態。
note.usage: 常用 reach/break an impasse、at an impasse。

noteEn.meaning: A situation where no progress is possible.
noteEn.usage: Common in 'reach an impasse' or 'break the impasse'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Los dos amigos llegaron a un punto muerto sobre las vacaciones.
noteEs.meaning: Situación en la que no se puede avanzar.

noteHi.exampleTr: छुट्टी की योजना पर दोनों दोस्तों में गतिरोध हो गया।
noteHi.meaning: ऐसी स्थिति जिसमें आगे बढ़ना संभव न हो; गतिरोध।
noteHi.usage: reach/break an impasse के रूप में आम।

noteJa.exampleTr: 2人の友人は休暇の計画で行き詰まった。
noteJa.meaning: 進展できない「行き詰まり、膠着状態」。
noteJa.usage: reach/break an impasse の形でよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 두 친구는 휴가 계획을 두고 교착 상태에 빠졌다.
noteKo.usage: reach/break an impasse 형태로 자주 쓴다.

in.en: inside; at a time or place

inadequate.en: not enough or not good enough
inadequate.ex: The heating was inadequate in winter.

example.en: The small room was inadequate for the meeting.
example.zh: 這間小房間不夠開會使用。

note.meaning: 「不足的、不夠好的」，數量或品質未達需要。
note.usage: 可放名詞前或作補語；常與 wholly/totally 連用加強語氣。

noteEn.meaning: Not enough, or not good enough.

noteEs.exampleTr: La sala pequeña era insuficiente para la reunión.
noteEs.meaning: Que no es suficiente o no es lo bastante bueno.
noteEs.usage: Se refuerza a menudo con «wholly» o «totally».

noteHi.exampleTr: छोटा कमरा बैठक के लिए अपर्याप्त था।
noteHi.meaning: मात्रा या गुणवत्ता में पर्याप्त नहीं।
noteHi.usage: wholly/totally जैसे शब्दों के साथ ज़ोर देने के लिए आता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: その小さな部屋は会議には不十分だった。
noteJa.meaning: 量や質が「不十分な、不適切な」。
noteJa.usage: wholly/totally などで強調されることが多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 작은 방은 회의를 하기에 부족했다.
noteKo.usage: wholly/totally 등과 함께 강조해서 자주 쓴다.

income.ex: Rent takes half of her income.

increases.ex: There was a sharp increase in prices.

independent.ex: An independent expert checked the data.

industrial.zh: 工業的；勞資的（industrial relations：勞資關係）

initiate.ex: The school will initiate a new reading program.

example.en: The city plans to initiate a recycling program.
example.zh: 市政府計劃啟動一項回收計畫。

note.meaning: 「發起、啟動」，正式地開始某項程序或行動。
note.usage: 較 start 正式，常接 talks、negotiations、proceedings 等名詞。

noteEn.usage: More formal than 'start'; often used with talks or action.

noteEs.exampleTr: La ciudad planea iniciar un programa de reciclaje.
noteEs.usage: Más formal que «start»; va con talks, negotiations, etc.

noteHi.exampleTr: शहर एक पुनर्चक्रण कार्यक्रम शुरू करने की योजना बना रहा है।
noteHi.meaning: औपचारिक रूप से कुछ शुरू करना।
noteHi.usage: start से अधिक औपचारिक; talks, negotiations के साथ।

noteJa.exampleTr: 市はリサイクル計画を開始する予定だ。
noteJa.meaning: 正式に「開始する、着手する」。
noteJa.usage: start より硬く、talks や negotiations などと結びつく。

noteKo.usage: start보다 격식 있으며 talks, negotiations 등과 쓴다.

insists.en: says firmly that something is true
insists.ex: She insists that she is right.

intensifies.ex: The heat intensifies in the afternoon.

example.en: The noise intensifies as the train gets closer.
example.zh: 火車越靠近，噪音就越大。

note.meaning: 「加劇、增強」，指壓力、競爭等變得更強烈。
note.usage: 可作不及物（pressure intensifies）或及物（intensify efforts）。

noteEn.usage: Can be used with or without an object.

noteEs.exampleTr: El ruido se intensifica a medida que el tren se acerca.
noteEs.usage: Puede ser intransitivo (pressure intensifies) o transitivo.

noteHi.exampleTr: ट्रेन के पास आने पर शोर तेज़ हो जाता है।
noteHi.meaning: और अधिक तेज़ या तीव्र होना।
noteHi.usage: अकर्मक (pressure intensifies) और सकर्मक दोनों रूपों में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 列車が近づくにつれて騒音が強まる。
noteJa.meaning: 圧力などが「強まる、激化する」。
noteJa.usage: 自動詞（pressure intensifies）にも他動詞にもなる。

intensive.en: involving a lot of effort in a short time
intensive.ex: She took an intensive English course.

invited.ex: They invited me to join the club.

is.en: exists or has a quality; also helps form verbs

issued.ex: The bank issued a warning about fake emails.

justification.ex: There is no justification for rudeness.

keep.en: keep up with: rise at the same rate as
keep.ex: Wages must keep up with prices.

last.ex: I saw her at the last meeting.

last-minute.en: done at the latest possible time

led.ex: The visitors were led into the hall.

lengths.en: go to lengths: try very hard
lengths.ex: He went to great lengths to find her.

letter.en: a written message sent to someone
letter.ex: I wrote a letter to my grandmother.

lies.ex: The answer lies in hard work.
lies.zh: 在於（lie at the crux of：是…的核心）

living.en: cost of living: money needed for daily life
living.ex: The cost of living in big cities is high.

look.ex: The team looks ready to win.
look.zh: 看起來（look poised to：看來即將）

lose.ex: The town could lose its charm.

loss.ex: The loss of forests harms wildlife.

lot.ex: I learned a lot from this course.

made.ex: The change will make life easier.

maintained.ex: The roads are maintained by the city.

maintains.en: says firmly that something is true
maintains.ex: She maintains that the plan will work.

major.ex: There are major roadworks in the city.

mediator.en: a person who helps two sides agree
mediator.ex: A mediator helped end the argument.

ministers.ex: The ministers met to discuss the budget.

more.en: a larger amount; more than: over

paragraphs: More than 300,000 public sector workers in Ireland plan to stop work for 24 hours on Wednesday, 14 October. Nurses, teachers and court workers will take part.
Hospitals and other important services will stay open.
The workers want more pay. They say prices went up faster than their pay. The unions say the gap is 5 to 7 per cent.
Minister Jack Chambers asked the unions to start talks. The unions said no in less than one hour. They say the Government has not changed its plan.
The Government says it gave €1.2 billion for pay in the budget. The unions say this is not enough. More one-day strikes may happen in the next eight days.

More than 300,000 public sector workers in Ireland are expected to go on strike for 24 hours on Wednesday, 14 October. Health workers, teachers and court staff are among those taking part. Essential services will continue.
On Monday, Jack Chambers, the Minister for Public Expenditure, invited the unions to talks at the Workplace Relations Commission. The unions rejected the offer very quickly.

In a letter, the minister said the strike would cause a lot of disruption and that workers would lose pay for no good reason. He said a deal could be reached quickly if both sides worked hard on it. He also pointed to the €1.2 billion for public sector pay in the budget.

The unions, led by Kevin Callinan of Fórsa, answered within an hour. They said the letter showed that the Government had not changed its position. They also said the Government had broken promises in the last national pay agreement, which ended in June.

The workers want a pay rise because prices have risen faster than wages. The unions say this gap is between 5 and 7 per cent. They also want to be sure that their pay will keep up with living costs in the future. They say €1.2 billion is far too little.

The Government says the budget also included help with the cost of living. Sources say relations between the minister's department and the unions have broken down. Further one-day strikes could follow in the next eight days.

More than 300,000 public sector workers, including healthcare staff, teachers and courts employees, are set to stage a 24-hour strike on Wednesday, 14 October, after a last-minute attempt to start negotiations failed. Essential services will be maintained.

Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers had offered to open talks at the Workplace Relations Commission, but union leaders swiftly turned down the proposal on Monday. The Government insists it has made serious efforts to engage and remains willing to attend talks.

In a letter to the public services committee of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions, chaired by Fórsa general secretary Kevin Callinan, Mr Chambers warned that the stoppage would cause major disruption and an avoidable loss of earnings. He argued that an agreement could be reached quickly through intensive engagement, and described the €1.2 billion set aside for public sector pay in the budget as significant.

The union officers responded within an hour, saying the letter contained no change in the Government's stance and offered no grounds for postponing the action. They accused the Government of failing to honour commitments made under the previous national agreement, which expired in June.

At the heart of the dispute is pay. Unions want increases to close a gap of 5 to 7 per cent between earlier wage rises and inflation, as well as a guarantee that salaries will not be eroded by rising living costs. They say the budget allocation falls well short.

Government sources admit that relations between the department and the unions have broken down. An independent mediator could be brought in, but this is considered unlikely until one or more of the planned stoppages has taken place.

More than 300,000 public servants – among them healthcare workers, teachers and courts staff – look poised to walk out for 24 hours on Wednesday, 14 October, after an eleventh-hour bid to get negotiations under way came to nothing. Essential services are to be safeguarded.

Jack Chambers, the Minister for Public Expenditure, had proposed convening talks at the Workplace Relations Commission, only for union leaders to rebuff the overture within hours on Monday. The Government maintains it has gone to considerable lengths to engage and stands ready to participate in talks.

Writing to the officers of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions' public services committee, chaired by Fórsa's Kevin Callinan, the minister cautioned that the stoppage would inflict severe disruption and needless loss of income on public servants. A settlement, he contended, was within reach if both sides committed to intensive engagement, and he characterised the €1.2 billion earmarked for public pay as a sizeable sum.

The unions' rejoinder arrived within the hour. The letter, they said, signalled no shift whatsoever in the Government's position and furnished no justification for calling off the action. They further accused ministers of reneging on commitments enshrined in the national agreement that lapsed in June.

Pay lies at the crux of the impasse. Unions are seeking increases to bridge a shortfall of 5 to 7 per cent between previous pay rises and inflation, together with a safeguard against wages being eroded by the soaring cost of living. In their view, the budget provision falls woefully short.

Sources on the Government side concede that the relationship has effectively broken down. Bringing in an independent mediator remains an option, though few expect such a move before the stoppages have run their course and public pressure mounts.

A substantial proportion of Ireland's public workforce – in excess of 300,000 employees across the health, education and courts sectors – is expected to participate in a 24-hour strike on Wednesday, 14 October, following the collapse of a final attempt to initiate negotiations. Essential services will nevertheless be maintained.

The Minister for Public Expenditure, Jack Chambers, had proposed that discussions take place under the auspices of the Workplace Relations Commission; however, union representatives promptly rejected this proposal. The Government, for its part, asserts that it has made considerable efforts to engage and remains prepared to enter talks.

In correspondence addressed to the public services committee of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions, chaired by Kevin Callinan of Fórsa, the minister argued that industrial action would result in significant disruption and an unnecessary loss of earnings. He maintained that a resolution could be achieved rapidly, contingent upon intensive engagement from both parties, and emphasised that the €1.2 billion allocated to public sector pay represented a considerable commitment.

The unions' response, issued within an hour, contended that the letter demonstrated no fundamental change in the Government's position and consequently provided no basis for postponement. Furthermore, they alleged that the Government had failed to fulfil obligations under the previous national agreement, which expired in June.

The dispute is fundamentally concerned with remuneration. The unions are seeking increases sufficient to offset a discrepancy of 5 to 7 per cent between earlier pay awards and inflation, in addition to assurances that wages will not deteriorate in real terms. They regard the budgetary allocation as wholly inadequate.

Sources within the Government acknowledge that relations have deteriorated markedly. Although the appointment of an independent mediator remains a possibility, it is considered improbable until the scheduled stoppages have occurred and public pressure intensifies.
